attack.failure: Treating available complete fastening families as freely combinable fails: pins cannot coexist with a non-pin retainer, and only one non-pin assembly may be installed. A claimed additive clip-plus-loop capacity has no supported opening. Component interactions must instead use the explicitly supported M/L or S/V interfaces.
attack.invariant: The same two panels retain at least 4 units at ticks 3, 4, 5, and 6 and separate with every installed retainer removed by boundary 10; no damage, discard, substitution, or outside resource.
attack.permitted_variable: Cross partial component mechanisms within one assembly: detached M with routed L, or detached S inserted into installed V. Select listed operations and their timing; capacities and exclusivity remain fixed.

budget_used.allocation: Declared before construction: six local concern passes: invariant lock; interface admissibility; M/L construction; S/V construction; timing and resources; burden, uncertainty, and refusal boundary. Maximum two constructions pursued within the cap of three; no fresh builder, helpers, historical reads, or retries.
budget_used.limits: Word caps are not equal compute. Six recorded local passes are one native role, not independent reviews or empirical trials.

candidates.burden: Six active operator ticks: three preparation, two removal, one restoration; four idle hold ticks. H is unavailable as an intact impact tool from boundary 1 until boundary 10; S remains free until restoration. Compared with the archived clip schedule this adds four active ticks; compared with two pins it adds two. No impact is used.
candidates.defeat: Routing before M is placed, using M while it remains part of H, delaying route past tick 2, releasing before required hold finishes, or failing to lift M before boundary 10 defeats the contract. No greater capacity can be inferred from extra turns of L.
candidates.lineage: Initial native N08 construction from J03/J07. No received candidate or dependency.
candidates.mechanism: Cross placed head M with routed loop L at the J07 head-loop interface. Detached M alone creates no retention; the stipulated mechanism requires both placement and routing. Route completion activates min(head 4, loop 4)=4. This changes intact-H impact fastening into one component-based retaining assembly; it does not combine complete retainers.
candidates.prediction: Modeled, pending root replay: detach completes at 1, placement at 2, routing at 3; retention is 4 throughout required ticks 3-6. Unrouting completes at 8, lifting at 9, and H restoration at 10. Relative to either partial component alone, the interaction enables the required retention; relative to the known clip it reduces no operator burden. No global originality or physical performance claim.

candidates.burden: Six active operator ticks and four idle hold ticks. Detaching H displaces all intact-H use until restoration at boundary 10; M stays free. Installing an incomplete sleeve assembly consumes the sole non-pin assembly place. Four more active ticks than archived clip fastening, two more than two-pin fastening; zero impacts.
candidates.defeat: If S is not detached/free at insertion, V is not installed, insertion completes after boundary 3, S is withdrawn before the hold finishes, or V remains installed at boundary 10, the construction fails. Sleeve and stem capacities cannot be added.
candidates.lineage: Initial alternate native N08 construction from J03/J06. No received candidate or dependency.
candidates.mechanism: Cross detached stem S with installed sleeve V at the J06 insertion interface. Neither free S nor V installation alone supplies the stipulated joint retention. Insertion completes one assembly with min(stem 4, sleeve 4)=4. The changed operation is disassembly and insertion instead of hammer impact.
candidates.prediction: Modeled, pending root replay: H detachment completes at 1, V installation at 2, insertion at 3. Retention is 4 over ticks 3-6. Withdrawal completes at 8, V removal at 9, H restoration at 10. Benefit is retention enabled by the interaction relative to its partial components, not superiority to the known clip. This is another supported construction outside the two listed archive entries, not proof of worldwide novelty.

handoff.residue: Both constructions require three preparation ticks and six active ticks including restoration. They use all three pre-hold preparation slots; H cannot simultaneously remain intact. The known clip takes only two active operations. Shared head/stem origin does not authorize combining M/L with S/V.
handoff.summary: N08 component interaction only. Replay either detach(H) at 0, place(M) at 1, route(L) at 2, unroute(L) at 7, lift(M) at 8, assemble(H) at 9; or detach(H) at 0, install(V) at 1, insert(S,V) at 2, withdraw(S,V) at 7, remove(V) at 8, assemble(H) at 9. Idle at 3-6. Operations complete at next boundary; one operator, one assembly, no pins or other retainers. Preserve 4 units for ticks 3-6 and all removals by 10. Q theta stays unknown and unused; refuse additive or extrapolated retention and unlisted actions. Predictions are finite-model constructions for root replay.

limits: Stipulated finite model, not measured physics; proposed action effects require root replay.
Local concern passes execute N08 but provide no independent review, grading, or comparative trial.
J10 establishes only two archive entries; non-archive constructions do not establish global novelty.
Default impact preference remains b=2; zero actual impacts need no ladder change. Hard capacities, resources, hold timing, and release boundary remain unchanged.
Q theta remains in {0,4}; no measurement, favorable assignment, or combination with another non-pin retainer is assumed.
No supported N08 opening combines complete pin and non-pin families or two non-pin assemblies. The interaction benefit is relative to partial components, with increased burden versus the clip.

operation_trace.result: Modeled hold through tick 6, first release completion at 8, final retainer removal at 9, restoration at 10. Only one action per tick; detached part locations prevent simultaneous H use. Root replay remains authoritative.
